summary: DRAFT for Rishi: A Rs 15 lakh degree in 13 years at 10% education inflation; does a Rs 12,000 SIP at 12% get there, and does a 5% yearly step-up? Three chained answers.
split_note: Placeholder: Rishi assigns discovery or held-out (D9).

messages.content: My daughter is 5. I want to save for her engineering degree, which I'll need when she turns 18. It costs about ₹15 lakh today, and education costs rise about 10% a year. What will it cost then? I can start a ₹12,000 monthly SIP that I expect to earn 12% a year: will that be enough? If not, would raising the SIP by 5% every year get me there?

graders.description: Open coding plus proposed yes/no criteria (DRAFT for Rishi); optional until the rubric and D7 are settled.

criteria.text: Would a real client in this situation be well served by this? Pass or fail, and one line on why.
Does the answer say plainly that ₹12,000 a month on its own falls short of the future cost? Yes or no.
Does the answer say that a 5% yearly step-up reaches the target? Yes or no.
Does the answer say that the 12% return is not guaranteed? Yes or no.

judge_criteria_to_write: Three chained answers: cost in 13 years 5178406.82 (present_value by mistake gives far less); SIP corpus 4511173.74, short; with a 5% step-up 5675167.91, enough. Gave-up-early shows as a missing step-up call and number.
